title: FLOT · chemotherapy before and after surgery
schedule_label: Four cycles → surgery → four cycles. Every 14 days during chemotherapy.
schedule_summary: Four cycles before surgery, then four after recovery. Each cycle is 14 days. Cycle 5 usually starts 6–12 weeks after the operation.
purpose: Shrink the cancer before surgery and treat microscopic cancer cells that could cause recurrence afterwards. The aim is cure.
indication_text: For resectable stomach or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, cT2 or higher or node positive (NCCP 00344). ESOPEC also studied resectable oesophageal adenocarcinoma.
administration_text: Four treatments two weeks apart. On day 1 you receive infusions and leave with a 24-hour fluorouracil pump. Your team disconnects it on day 2.
monitoring_summary: Repeat blood counts, kidney and liver tests. Report tingling or numbness. The team assesses nerves at least every two cycles and sooner if needed.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: It holds the structures used in cell division in place so dividing cells cannot separate.
agents.mechanism: It holds the structures used in cell division in place so dividing cells cannot separate.
agents.watch: Call urgently for fever or sudden illness. During the drip, report flushing, wheeze or dizziness.
risks: Hair and nail changes, fluid retention
symptoms: Hair and nail changes, fluid retention
visual: It holds the structures used in cell division in place so dividing cells cannot separate.

agents.name: Oxaliplatin
agents.explanation: It links strands of DNA, making it harder for cells to copy them.
agents.mechanism: It links strands of DNA, making it harder for cells to copy them.
agents.watch: Tell the team about numb fingers, falls or difficulty buttoning clothes. Report throat tightness or breathing difficulty immediately.
visual: It links strands of DNA, making it harder for cells to copy them.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: It interferes with the building blocks cells need to make DNA and RNA. A pump gives it over 24 hours.
agents.mechanism: It interferes with the building blocks cells need to make DNA and RNA. A pump gives it over 24 hours.
agents.watch: Chest pain needs immediate assessment. Phone early for mouth ulcers, diarrhoea or painful hands and feet.
risks: Heart spasm or chest pain, severe early toxicity in DPD deficiency
symptoms: Heart spasm or chest pain, severe early toxicity in DPD deficiency
visual: It interferes with the building blocks cells need to make DNA and RNA. A pump gives it over 24 hours.

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: It helps fluorouracil block a DNA-making enzyme for longer.
agents.mechanism: It helps fluorouracil block a DNA-making enzyme for longer.
agents.watch: It can increase the bowel and mouth effects of fluorouracil. Report a rash, swelling or wheeze during infusion.
visual: It helps fluorouracil block a DNA-making enzyme for longer.

common_effects.title: Cold sensitivity and numbness
common_effects.text: Cold drinks or cold air can trigger tingling after oxaliplatin. Use warm layers and room-temperature drinks. Report symptoms that persist between cycles.

common_effects.title: Mouth, bowel and skin
common_effects.text: Use the mouth care your unit recommends and report soreness, loose stools, painful palms or soles early. Phone if you cannot drink.

common_effects.title: Fatigue and eating after surgery
common_effects.text: Small frequent meals and drinks can be easier. Contact your dietitian if your weight falls or feeds are difficult. Ask about support for fatigue.

serious_effects.title: Fever or sudden illness
serious_effects.text: A low white cell count can allow infection to progress quickly. Call your 24-hour oncology number immediately for a fever at the threshold your unit gave you, chills or feeling suddenly unwell, even without a fever.

serious_effects.title: Chest pain or trouble breathing
serious_effects.text: Fluorouracil can affect the heart. During a drip alert the nurse immediately. At home seek urgent help. Call 112 or 999 for severe chest pain or breathing difficulty.

serious_effects.title: Severe early diarrhoea or mouth ulcers
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently if symptoms are severe, especially in the first cycle, or if you cannot drink. These may signal severe fluorouracil toxicity.

serious_effects.title: Pump or line trouble
serious_effects.text: Phone the unit promptly for swelling, pain, a wet dressing, leakage or a pump that finishes much earlier or later than planned. Follow your unit’s spill instructions.

phases.label: Before surgery
phases.detail: Four treatments two weeks apart. On day 1 you receive infusions and leave with a 24-hour fluorouracil pump. Your team disconnects it on day 2.

phases.label: Surgery and recovery
phases.detail: The surgeon and oncology team review healing, infection, swallowing, fluid and food intake, weight and strength. The operation sets the timing of the next phase.

phases.label: After surgery
phases.detail: Cycle 5 usually starts 6–12 weeks after surgery, once you have recovered. The team confirms the restart date. Four further cycles are planned two weeks apart if tolerated.

anatomy: Report ulcers early. Phone if you cannot drink.
Cold may trigger throat sensations. Alert the team immediately for breathing or swallowing difficulty.
New chest pain needs urgent assessment. Call 112 or 999 for severe pain.
Tell the nurse immediately about pain, swelling or leakage at the line.
Call urgently for severe cramps, fever, loose stools or blood.
Fever, chills or sudden illness may be infection. Call now.
Report burning, redness, peeling or painful soles.
Report tingling, weakness or numbness that affects buttons or walking.
anatomy_note: Call your treating team about new or worsening symptoms.

questions.a: Write down day 1, the day 2 pump visit, your surgery date and your planned cycle 5 review.
The team reviews recovery, symptoms and the follow-up plan. Ask how to contact the upper gastrointestinal team between visits.

support.title: Docetaxel steroid tablets
support.text: Take prescribed dexamethasone beginning the day before each infusion. Bring the times and doses taken. If you miss a dose, ring before attending. The team reconciles this with anti-sickness steroids.

support.title: Nausea or vomiting
support.text: Follow your signed anti-sickness prescription. Contact the unit if vomiting continues or fluids will not stay down.

support.title: Infection prevention
support.text: After a fever with low white cells or a treatment delay from low white cells, your team may prescribe growth-factor injections. Confirm the dates with your team.

support.title: Fatigue and eating after surgery
support.text: Small frequent meals and drinks can be easier. Contact your dietitian if your weight falls or feeds are difficult. Ask about support for fatigue.

teachback: When is your pump disconnected, and who will confirm the date of your first cycle after surgery?
consent_support: Discuss benefits, alternatives, lasting nerve symptoms, fertility and the option to defer or decline.
safety_note: Phone oncology immediately for fever, chills, sudden illness, severe diarrhoea, or a leaking pump. Call 112 or 999 for severe chest pain, collapse or severe breathing difficulty.
urgent_extra: Phone oncology immediately for fever, chills, sudden illness, severe diarrhoea, or a leaking pump. Call 112 or 999 for severe chest pain, collapse or severe breathing difficulty.

evidence.title: FLOT4 and ESOPEC
evidence.interpretation: In FLOT4, median survival was 50 months with perioperative FLOT and 35 months with older chemotherapy. In ESOPEC, 57.4% were alive at three years with FLOT versus 50.7% with preoperative chemoradiotherapy.
evidence.limitations: These trials compared whole treatment strategies. They cannot quantify the benefit of an individual postoperative cycle or predict one person’s outcome.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before first cycle
cells: Blood counts, kidney and liver function and a dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) test. Low DPD activity can make fluorouracil dangerous.
Tell us about earlier reactions and bring a medication list.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: Repeat blood counts, kidney and liver tests. Report tingling or numbness. The team assesses nerves at least every two cycles and sooner if needed.
Tell us about fever, sore mouth, diarrhoea or trouble using your hands.

rows.label: Before cycle 5
cells: Surgical recovery, eating and drinking, weight, activity, blood results and lasting side effects.
Contact the surgical or oncology team if swallowing worsens, feeds are difficult or you feel unwell.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team plans scans and follow-up according to your treatment and recovery.

sections.title: Day before treatment
sections.text: Check the steroid prescription and bring your medication list.

sections.title: Connecting the pump
sections.text: The day unit attaches your 24-hour fluorouracil pump to your line on day 1. Confirm where and when your trained team will disconnect it on day 2.

sections.title: At home with the pump
sections.text: Keep the line secure, dry and free of kinks. Follow your unit’s instructions for sleeping and washing. Leave disconnection and any change to the flow to your trained team.

sections.title: Pump or line trouble
sections.text: Phone the unit promptly for swelling, pain, a wet dressing, leakage or a pump that finishes much earlier or later than planned. Follow your unit’s spill instructions.
